Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

Evidence supports testing the loss before changing SASRec’s architecture. [gSASRec, summarized at IJCAI 2024](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939), combines multiple random negatives with calibrated generalized BCE to address sampling-induced overconfidence; it provides a useful control against attributing all gains to softmax. [Scalable Cross-Entropy, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18721), approximates full-catalog CE using maximum-inner-product retrieval of informative items, reporting up to 100× lower peak memory while retaining or improving recommendation quality. These results motivate multi-negative objectives but do not establish gains on the pinned Electronics task.

Hardest-negative selection can hurt through false negatives and excessive difficulty early in training. [R²NS, WWW 2026](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf), compares samplers across five sequential backbones and BCE/BPR objectives. Its SASRec experiments show that uniform warm-up before hard mining improves over immediate hard mining. The method combines warm-up, efficient global retrieval, and progressively harder stochastic selection; sampling among top-ranked candidates reduces dependence on a single potentially false negative. [Author implementation](https://github.com/Lyz103/R2NS).

Affordable proposed ablation: keep SASRec fixed; compare single-negative BCE, multi-negative BCE/gBCE, and sampled softmax with 16–64 uniform negatives. Only then test a small hard-negative fraction after warm-up, selecting randomly among several high-scoring candidates. Exclude padding, the target, and known training positives; this removes observed-positive collisions but cannot identify all false negatives. Treat these settings as experimental proposals. Select using the exact four-category macro validation HR@10, inspect Electronics separately, and record GPU cost; training margins and published results cannot substitute for this validation.

Recent work supports separating similarity from complementarity. [SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) models complementary graphs with low-pass filters for relevance and mid-pass filters for dissimilarity, combining them through attention. This offers a useful architectural pattern, but requires a complementary graph; purchase sequences alone do not establish relation labels. [DAKSR (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.is.2024.102470) injects explicit item correlations into Transformer attention and contrastive augmentation, while [KGSCL (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2025.107191) uses knowledge-guided insertion/substitution and co-occurrence sampling. Both depend on knowledge relations unavailable in the stated benchmark, so their graph construction cannot be adopted directly.

For local text encoding, an older relevant precedent is a [Siamese BiLSTM using titles/descriptions](https://aclanthology.org/2020.ecnlp-1.3/), supervised by customer comparison behavior. That supervision is also unavailable here; the reusable component is the text-encoder design, with randomly initialized token embeddings as a proposed adaptation. A benchmark-compatible hypothesis is to combine SASRec with separate text-similarity and directed, time-windowed transition channels, learning their weights per category using training interactions. Treat these as uncertain relation proxies: co-occurrence does not prove complementarity, and textual similarity does not prove substitutability. Equipment titles may expose model numbers and compatibility clues, but compatibility needs explicit textual evidence. For movies/music, artist, franchise, format and edition overlap may indicate either preference continuity or redundant purchases; avoid blanket similarity penalties. These are proposed adaptations, not demonstrated gains—select using the prescribed macro validation HR@10.

---

Recent work supports separating persistent preferences from current intent. [LSIDN (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) uses separate encoders and denoising strategies: session-level interest evolution for long-term preferences, contrastive augmentation for short-term noise. [D2MFRec (2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-31190-z) combines global sequence modeling, recent-item attention, soft clustering into multiple interests, and learned fusion gates. [DSRec (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21548) explicitly uses historical aggregation for stable preferences and inter-click time intervals for local intent, with separate state-space encoders and residual cross-fusion.

The closest match to satisfied purchase intent is [Learning to Forget (SIGIR 2026 Industry Track)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12714). Its satiation-aware mechanism suppresses historical clicks associated with completed purchases, learns replenishment rhythms, and applies a time-sensitive gate that inhibits satisfied interests before gradually reactivating them. A time-to-next-purchase auxiliary objective learns product lifecycles. Its click/purchase distinction requires signals beyond an undifferentiated interaction history; an interaction alone cannot establish that a need was fulfilled.

For this benchmark, a practical hypothesis is a recent-window intent encoder plus several persistent-interest vectors, fused through a learned gate conditioned on observed time gaps, recent/history agreement, and sequence length. Optional decay or recovery of latent interests could approximate intent lifecycles using histories alone, but should be treated as an inferred mechanism, not observed satisfaction. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec encodes interaction sequences with item embeddings, learned positional embeddings, and causal self-attention blocks. Each position predicts the next item through a dot product with shared item embeddings. Attention lets predictions draw on recent actions or longer histories. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
